sections.skill: Explain the context window and what happens when it is exceeded

questions.prompt: What is a context window?

choices.text: The time of day when the model is available
The limited amount of text a model can use at once
The window on screen where the app is shown
The list of every fact the model learned

questions.correct_answer: The limited amount of text a model can use at once
questions.intro: A model can only consider a limited amount of text at once, called its CONTEXT WINDOW, measured in tokens. The context usually includes instructions the product adds, the conversation so far, any files or pasted text, and the reply being written. When a long conversation or document exceeds the window, something has to give: depending on the product, older messages may be dropped or shortened, part of a file may be left out, or the request may be refused. The model cannot use text that is no longer in its context, so it may "forget" early details or miss the end of a long document.
questions.feedback: Context is the text the model can use right now.

sections.skill: Compare the context window with a whiteboard

questions.prompt: In the comparison, what is the whiteboard like?

choices.text: The model's training data
The user's keyboard
The company office
The context window

questions.correct_answer: The context window
questions.intro: Imagine a WHITEBOARD in a meeting room. Everything the group is discussing must be written on it to be used. The board is big but not endless. When it fills up, someone erases the oldest notes to make room, and from then on the group cannot look at what was erased. A model's context window works like the board: instructions, the conversation and any pasted text are "written" there. When it fills, older material may be removed, and the model can no longer use it.
questions.feedback: The board holds what is in use now.

questions.prompt: What happens when the board fills up?

choices.text: All notes are kept

sections.skill: Help a model use long input well

questions.prompt: A long report fits in the context, but the answer misses a key figure in the middle. What does this show?

choices.text: Models never read the middle of documents
The figure must not exist in the report
Fitting in the window does not ensure careful use
Context windows are always unlimited

questions.correct_answer: Fitting in the window does not ensure careful use
questions.intro: Even text that fits in the context window is not always used equally well. Models can overlook details buried in the middle of a very long input, especially when many similar details compete. Practical habits help: put the most important instructions and facts where they are easy to find, restate key requirements when a conversation gets long, split very long documents into sections, and check that answers cover the parts you care about. A bigger context window raises the limit; it does not guarantee careful reading.
questions.feedback: Details in the middle can be overlooked.
